items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law and the agriculture and markets law, in relation to therapy dogs and cats for persons with disabilities
items.lawCode: Amd §§292, 296 & 356, Exec L; amd §108, Ag & Mkts L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5080

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the executive law and the
agriculture and markets law, in relation to therapy dogs and cats for
persons with disabilities

 PURPOSE :

This bill provides that persons with disabilities may not be subjected
to housing discrimination for living with a therapy dog or cat.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: amends subdivision 21 of section 292 of the executive law
to include that a condition which substantially limits one or more of
a person's major life activities is a disability.

Major life activities include a list of human functions, both
operative and cognitive, as well as bodily functions.

Section 2: amends subdivision of section 296 of the executive law to
include service dogs of any breed and therapy dogs or cats within the
class of animals protected from unlawful discriminatory practices.

Section 3: amends subdivision 26 of section 108 of the agriculture and
markets law to include therapy cats within the existing definition of
therapy dogs and to include personal residences within places therapy
dogs and cats are protected.

Section 4: amends subdivision 1 of section 356 of the executive law to
include housing services, not limited to instances of discrimination,
within the state veterans' service agency's powers and duties to
inform.

Section 5: effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The federal Fair Housing Act (42 USC 3602, et seq) protects persons
with a disability from housing discrimination based on that
disability. While New York State Human Rights Law has recognized many
of these protections, individuals with disabilities, especially
returning veterans suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder.
(PTSD) who rely on medically-prescribed therapy dogs or cats, are
still being denied housing or are being forced to leave adequate
housing due to the presence of their therapy animal in the home.

Federal and state agencies charged with implementing the Fair Housing
Act (including the NY Attorney General's Civil Rights Bureau, NYS
Division of Human Rights, and U.S. Department of Justice) have
recognized that individuals with therapy and emotional support animals
must be reasonably accommodated. Yet, veterans living with PTS
throughout New York state are targeted for their therapy dogs and cats
and denied otherwise publicly-available housing.

According to a 2011 RAND Corporation study, PTSD or combat-related
depression affects approximately 22 percent of Iraq and Afghanistan
veterans.(1) In another report, according to Veteran's Affairs
facilities, roughly 30 percent of post-9/11 veterans treated at these
medical departments have screened positive for PTSD. (2) Finally, a
Stanford University study projects that in the coming years, upwards
of 35 percent of all veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan will suffer from
PTSD and other mental illnesses following their deployment.(3) These
figures affect people from every part of New York State. This
legislation is in response to concerns raised by a local veterans
services agency regarding the denial of housing-or an eviction based
on the presence of a therapy dog or cat in the home, which is often
utilized in a treatment plan for veterans with PTSD. These local
heroes may then face homelessness or must rely on the nearest VA
hospital for housing until they can find a place that will accommodate
their therapy dog or cat, which provides them with critical therapy
and support.

In order to correct this injustice and close this loophole, this
legislation codifies outlying portions of the federal Fair Housing Act
into New York State law to afford more complete, explicit protections
on not only persons with disabilities, but particularly veterans
suffering from PTSD. After these young men and women serve our
country, it is our duty to protect their right to be safely and
adequately housed when they return home.

(1) http://www.rand.org/content/dam/rand/pubs/technical_reports/2011/
RAND TR920.pdf

(2) http://www.militarytimes.com/story/military/benefits/healthcare/
2015/05/10/ptsd-service-dogs-va-perdue/70944650/

(3)
http://www.gillibrand.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/Sen.%20Gillibrand%20
PTSD%20andt20TBIt20Report.pdf

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
